I've switched to Samsung this year, and I'm genuinely rooting for them. I want them to succeed because competition is good. But the more I use it, the more I realize Apple's biggest advantage has never been hardware—it's the software experience.

Samsung wins on paper with specs, but it's the little things that make Apple feel more complete. Features like the charging dock mode, polished UI, seamless wallpapers and themes, and all the small quality-of-life touches add up. It feels like Samsung is trying to beat Apple on hardware when software is where the real gap still exists.

That said, Apple isn't perfect either. Their file transfer system has always been frustrating. Instead of embracing open standards like Bluetooth, they've pushed users toward AirDrop and their own ecosystem. On top of that, you have to buy the expensive Pro models to get many of the headline features.

For now, I'm sticking with Samsung because I want to explore what Android has to offer. The Z Fold 8 looks interesting, but software is still my biggest concern. If Samsung doesn't convince me, I might give the Pixel Pro a try next year.
